name: Shock hitting a helium bubble
blurb: A Mach 1.22 shock in air runs into a bubble of helium (with 28% air by mass), after Haas & Sturtevant (1987) and Quirk & Karni (1996). Each gas has its own gamma. The light bubble is flattened, turned into a vortex pair (a ring in 3D), and pierced by a jet of air along the axis.

featured.label: Shock Mach number
featured.tip: Mach number of the shock in the air. Changing it starts the run again

featured.label: Helium in the bubble
featured.tip: Mass fraction of helium in the bubble, the rest air (0.72 in the experiment, where the bubble took in some air). Changing it starts the run again

featured.label: Bubble radius
featured.tip: Radius of the bubble, in units of the tube width. Changing it starts the run again
